            HON'BLE DR. SRIKANT PANDEY              :    MEMBER

 

           

 

 COUNSEL FOR PARTIES :

 

                Shri Pankaj Waghmode, learned counsel for the appellants.

 

           Shri Ajay Dubey, learned counsel for the respondent.

 

 

 

 O R D E R
(Passed On 30.04.2024)

 

                        The following order of the Commission was delivered by A. K. Tiwari, Acting President:
This appeal by the opposite parties/appellants-National Insurance Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as 'insurance
-2-
company') is directed against the order dated 26.05.2016 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Rewa (for short the 'District Commission') in C. C. No. 193/2015 whereby the complaint filed by the complainant/respondent has been allowed.
2.                Briefly put, facts of the case as narrated by the complainant are that after taking finance from the Tata Motors Finance had purchased a Tata vehicle registration no. MP-17 HH-3771 which was insured with the opposite party no.3-insurance company for the period w.e.f. 08.02.2014 to 07.02.2015 for IDV of Rs.19,20,000/-.  On 09.12.2014 during currency of the policy period, his vehicle after colliding with a tree overturned and got damaged of which intimation was given to the insurance company on 09.02.2014. The insurance company appointed surveyor in the matter. The agent of the insurance company assured him to get the claim settled within a month. The complainant incurred Rs.3,69,690/- in repairs of the subject vehicle. It is submitted that the complainant's vehicle was being driven by the driver having valid and effective driving licence.   The claim filed with the insurance company was repudiated by the insurance company on 18.06.2015. The complainant therefore, alleging deficiency in service on part of opposite parties, filed complaint before the District Commission, seeking compensation of Rs.3,69,690/- with costs of Rs.15,000/-
-3-
3.                The opposite parties-insurance company admitting receiving of intimation, survey of the subject vehicle and denial of claim denied the other allegations made in the complaint. It is submitted that as per documents made available by the complainant, the subject vehicle was having permit authorization for the period w.e.f. 07.03.2013 to 06.03.2014 and the subject vehicle met with an accident on 09.12.2014 and therefore at the time of accident was running without having any valid permit authorization and therefore, the complainant's claim is not payable.
4.                The District Commission holding that there is no such condition in the policy document that vehicle cannot run without permit, the repudiation of claim by the insurance company amounts to deficiency in service and therefore allowed the complaint directing the insurance company to pay Rs.1,57,475/- with interest @8% p.a. from the date of filing of complaint till payment. Costs of Rs.1,000/- is also awarded.
5.                Heard. Perused the record.
6.                Learned counsel for the opposite parties/appellants-insurance company argued that if the complainant was having valid permit authorization, he could have filed the same. He argued that the District Commission has committed grave error in not considering the fact that the complainant's vehicle being a transport vehicle cannot run on road without having valid permit authorization. He argued that as per provisions of
-4-
Motor Vehicles Act
, the period of validity of an authorization shall not exceed one year at a time. The subject vehicle was having valid permit authorization for the period w.e.f. 07.03.2013 to 06.03.2014 and the subject vehicle met with an accident on 09.12.2014 and therefore at the time of accident was running without having any valid permit authorization. The insurance company has rightly repudiated the claim as the complainant's claim was not payable. There has been no deficiency in service on part of the insurance company. He placed reliance on the decisions of this Commission in Appeal No.542/2007 (
National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Smt. Sonia Lalchandani
) decided on 19.12.2007 and in First Appeal No.142/2017 (
National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Sandeep Khemka
) decided on 11.01.2023.
7.                Learned counsel for the complainant/appellant argued that the District Commission rightly considering the fact that no such condition is mentioned in the policy that a transport vehicle cannot run without valid permit authorization, the insurance company has committed deficiency in service in repudiating the claim. He argued that the District Commission has rightly allowing the complaint directed the insurance company to pay compensation and costs.
-5-
8.                Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on going through the impugned order, the record of the District Commission and the provisions of the
Motor Vehicles Act
, we find that it has been categorically submitted by the opposite parties/appellants-insurance company that the subject vehicle at the time of accident was being driven without valid permit authorization and this was the ground for repudiation taken by the insurance company in their repudiation letter.
9.
Section 66
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which deals with 'Necessity for permits' is relevant for deciding the issue involved in the matter which reads thus:
Section 66
. Necessity for permits:
(1).....
(2) .....
(3) The provisions of sub-section (1) shall not apply--
(i) to any goods vehicle, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 3,000 kilograms;
(p) to any transport vehicle while proceeding empty to any place for purpose of repair;
10.
Section 66(3)(p)
provides that the provision of permit do not apply to any transport vehicle, while proceeding empty to any place for purpose of repair. This sub-section is not applicable in the instant matter since it pertains to the empty transport vehicle and relying on this sub-section makes it amply clear that the empty transport vehicle as that of the complainant/appellant, can be run without permit only when it is taken to any place for purpose of repair.
-6-
11.              In the instant matter, the subject vehicle was insured with the opposite party insurance company for the period 08.02.2014 to 07.02.2015 for IDV of Rs.19,20,000/- under the policy (C-1). The complainant has filed National Permit (C-24) valid for the period w.e.f.07.03.2013 to 06.03.2018. On the other hand, the insurance company has also filed the aforesaid document as D-5. The insurance company has filed authorization for National Permit in Form 45 (Under Rule 83(2) and Rule 87(2) of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989) for All India (D-6) but that authorization is valid for the period w.e.f. 07.03.2013 to 06.03.2014 and the accident took place on 09.12.2014.  The insurance company has filed D-7 investigation report dated 09.12.2014 wherein investigator Suresh Kumar Singh also opined that the authorization for All India Permit was valid for the period w.e.f. 07.03.2013 to 06.03.2014. D-9 is the certificate dated 23.03.2015 provided by the RTO Rewa wherein it has been specifically stated that the subject vehicle MP-17 HH-3771 was not having valid authorization of permit for MP on the date of accident i.e. 09.12.2014.
12.              It is also pertinent to mention here that Rule 87(3) of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 specifically provided that the period of validity of an authorization shall not exceed one year at a time. From the above it is clearly established that on the date of accident i.e. 09.12.2014 the
-7-
subject vehicle was not having valid authorization of permit. The subject vehicle being used without valid authorization of permit which is fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy as also the provisions of
Section 66(1)
of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.
13.              Hon'ble National Commission in
Sudershan Giri Vs United India Insurance Company Limited & Anr
IV (2020) CPJ 3 (NC)Sudershan Giri
(supra) has clearly held that vehicle being used without valid permit is fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy as also provisions of
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
.
14.              From the evidence on record, we find that admittedly, the complainant was using the subject vehicle without having a valid permit authorisation, which amounts to clear violation of
Section 66(1)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 as also a fundamental breach of policy terms and conditions. Thus, we find that the insurance company has not committed any deficiency in service while repudiating the claim on account of violation of fundamental breach of policy terms and conditions as also the provisions of
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
.
15.              Therefore, in view of the aforesaid and on the basis of provisions of law, we find that the District Commission has gravely erred in holding the insurance company deficient in service for repudiation of claim
-8-
on the ground that the subject vehicle was not having valid authorization of All India Permit at the time of accident and the complainant's vehicle could

 

run without permit since there is no such condition in the policy document. We do not find any deficiency in service on part of the insurance company in repudiating the claim.
16.              In view of the aforesaid, the impugned order cannot be sustained. Accordingly, it is hereby set-aside. Consequently, the complaint is dismissed.
17.              In the result, this appeal succeeds and is hereby allowed with no order as to costs.
(A. K. Tiwari)                          (Dr. Srikant Pandey)

 

            Acting President                              Member
